criteria.TP: The finding holds against the text of the requirements it cites.
criteria.BORDERLINE: Defensible but resting on one reading of an underspecified requirement, or extrapolating beyond what the requirements entail.
criteria.FP: The finding does not hold. Includes gaps whose supposedly missing requirement is present elsewhere in the collection.

format: key = C<cluster>|<category>|<index>; value = VERDICT or VERDICT|reason

verdicts.C1|gaps|1: FP|the communication standard is specified by R25, 'The system must support both the European communication standard (ETSI ITS-G5) and the cellular network-based one (C-V2X)'.
verdicts.C6|inconsistencies|1: FP|the two budgets govern different components and different scopes: R33 bounds detection by road sensors, R12 bounds identification plus transmission to emergency services by cameras. Both can hold at once.
verdicts.C6|gaps|1: FP|wrong-way detection is specified by R135 and R99, which the alert of R8 can rely on.
verdicts.C0|gaps|1: FP|the underlying mechanisms are specified elsewhere: R22 requires authentication certificates, R44 and R23 require encryption of all vehicle-infrastructure communications.
verdicts.C10|inconsistencies|1: BORDERLINE|a feasibility concern rather than a contradiction, and hedged as such: R47 counts from entry into the payment lane, not from the gantry, so the three constraints are not shown to be jointly unsatisfiable.
verdicts.C4|gaps|1: BORDERLINE|an MTBF figure is a reasonable engineering addition but is not entailed by the availability and recovery targets already stated; the prompt restricts gaps to what existing requirements strongly imply.
verdicts.C7|inconsistencies|1: FP|R55 bounds the latency of the reply to a request, R66 the refresh interval of the source data; a reply delivered in 5 seconds carrying data up to 10 seconds old satisfies both.
verdicts.C5|inconsistencies|2: FP|R63 sets a lower bound of 365 days, which unlimited retention satisfies rather than contradicts; the two also govern different data.
verdicts.C2|dependencies|1: BORDERLINE|the relation is hedged as 'could be enabled by' and the two requirements address different events; nothing in R96 presupposes R110.
